newsitem.title: ITALY: Anti-landmine campaigners want full Italian ban.
newsitem.headline: Anti-landmine campaigners want full Italian ban.

text.p: Disarmament campaigners called on Italy on Monday to enshrine in law a pledge to end the production and export of anti-personnel landmines.

Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told the U.N. General Assembly in New York last Thursday that Italy would renounce the production and export of landmines "once and for all" and begin destroying existing devices.
Nicoletta Dentico, national coordinator of the Italian Campaign Against Mines, welcomed Dini's statement but said the group wanted the government to clarify how it planned to carry out the pledge.
Italy has been singled out in the past by the United Nations as a key producer of many of the 110 million landmines planted worldwide, along with China, Bulgaria and other nations.
Dentico called on the government to draft a law banning the production and export of landmines and also the transfer of technology that allowed them to be made in other countries.
She also said the government should help pay for the dismantling of landmines and give aid for the rehabilitation of people injured by landmine explosions.
"We should pay compensation for some of the damage we've done," Dentico said.
